title: A divisor's dividend is congruent to zero modulo it
statement: For naturals a and b: if a divides b then b is congruent to 0 modulo a.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.mod_eq_zero_of_dvd : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat.dvd x0 x1) -> AxNat.modEq x0 x1 AxNat.zero)))

evidence.supports: Nat.mod_eq_zero_of_dvd is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: test "$(cargo run -q -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example nat_theorem_inventory -- Nat.mod_eq_zero_of_dvd 2>/dev/null | grep -Ec '^Nat\.mod_eq_zero_of_dvd[[:space:]]')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: `build_nat_prelude` admits this theorem only through the trusted kernel gate, so a successful build IS the type-check; the command both performs it and prints the admitted type, which is copied verbatim into formal.statement.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the Nat environment admits no trusted declaration

The enumeration is per-environment, not per-theorem; it bounds this theorem's footprint because a proof cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain.
